html:
In an Indian household, life often happens at floor level. Whether it is sitting down for a family meal, performing daily puja, or using a traditional squat-style washroom, these movements are second nature to us.

For a patient suffering from chronic hip pain, the fear isn’t just about the surgery itself; it is the fear of losing this cultural way of life. The question we often hear at Silver Touch Hospitals is: If I get a new hip, will I be restricted to chairs and Western toilets forever?

The reality is that while a hip replacement is designed to give you back your mobility, the new joint has mechanical boundaries. At Silver Touch Hospitals, we explain to our patients that sitting on the floor or squatting puts the hip joint in a position of extreme flexion. In simpler terms, when you bend your hip too deeply, there is a risk of the ball slipping out of the socket (dislocation). Because of this, we generally advise against sitting on the floor or using traditional toilets in the months following your hip replacement surgery in Ahmedabad.

However, this doesn’t mean you are grounded forever; it means your body needs time and training to handle these movements safely.

Essential Precautions for a Safe Recovery

To ensure your new hip lasts for decades, you must follow specific safety protocols, especially during the first six months. Our doctors at Silver Touch Hospitals recommend the following precautions:

  • The 90-degree rule: Always ensure your knees stay lower than your hips when sitting. Avoid low sofas or stools that force your hips to bend too sharply.
  • Avoid crossing legs: Crossing your legs at the knees or ankles can put undue pressure on the surgical site and increase the risk of instability.
  • Modify your washroom: We strongly suggest installing a raised toilet seat or using a Western-style commode to avoid the deep squatting required by traditional washrooms.
  • Pivot, don’t twist: When turning around, move your whole body rather than twisting at the waist or hip.
  • Use support: When attempting to sit lower, always use the armrests of a chair or a sturdy support to lower yourself gently.

While it is possible for some patients to eventually return to sitting on a low stool or the floor after full recovery, it must always be done with extreme caution and with the okay from your surgeon. Choosing an experienced team for hip replacement surgery in Ahmedabad ensures that you receive the right physiotherapy to strengthen the muscles that make these movements possible.

Don’t let fear hold you back!

You should not let the fear of lifestyle changes hold you back from a pain-free life. A hip replacement at Silver Touch Hospitals is meant to end your suffering and get you back on your feet. If you are worried about how surgery will change your daily routine, come visit us for a detailed consultation. We will assess your specific needs and help you plan a recovery that respects both your health and your lifestyle.
